message.content:
Based on my search, here are the main ways to pay federal taxes online:

## 1. IRS Direct Pay (Free)
- **Website**: [directpay.irs.gov](https://www.irs.gov/payments/direct-pay-with-bank-account)
- Pay directly from your checking or savings account
- No registration required, but identity verification is needed using your prior-year tax return information
- Available Monday-Saturday (midnight to 11:45 p.m. EST) and Sunday (7 a.m. to 11:45 p.m. EST)
- Can schedule payments up to 365 days in advance
- Can modify or cancel payments up to two business days before processing

## 2. Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS) (Free)
- **Website**: [www.eftps.gov](https://www.eftps.gov)
- Requires enrollment and a PIN mailed to you
- Available 24/7 for individuals, businesses, and federal agencies
- Schedule payments up to a year in advance
- Track payment history for up to 16 months
- **Note**: EFTPS no longer accepts new users; existing users are being transitioned to IRS online accounts or Direct Pay

## 3. IRS Online Account
- Access through [IRS.gov](https://www.irs.gov)
- Manage and make payments through your personal IRS account

## 4. Debit/Credit Card or Digital Wallet (Fees Apply)
- Processed through third-party providers:
  - **Pay1040**: [pay1040.com](https://www.pay1040.com)
  - **ACI Payments** (formerly Official Payments)
- **Debit card**: Flat fee of approximately $2.10-$2.15
- **Credit card**: 1.75%-1.85% of payment amount (minimum $2.50)
- Also available through the IRS2Go mobile app

## 5. Electronic Funds Withdrawal (EFW) (Free)
- Available when e-filing through tax software or with a tax professional
- Authorize direct debit from your bank account when filing your return
- Can schedule payments until your return due date

## 6. IRS2Go Mobile App (Free App, Card Fees Apply)
- Download for iOS or Android
- Make payments via mobile version of Direct Pay (free) or with debit/credit card (fees apply)

## Important Recent Change
As of March 25, 2025, an Executive Order requires federal tax payments to be made electronically. Paper checks and money orders will no longer be accepted after **September 30, 2025**. Fourth quarter 2025 estimated tax payments (due January 15, 2026) must be submitted electronically.

Sources:
